Live burden: The reply directly answers Sharpton’s personal confirmation without denying its psychological reality, but must still demonstrate why naturalistic alternatives explain the experience better than the strongest theistic interpretation. Strongest feature: Hitchens answers Sharpton’s counterexample unambiguously and even-handedly: he concedes secular atrocities, identifies historically-inherited quasi-divine obedience as a mechanism Stalin could exploit, and consistently rejects authoritarian-political as well as religious idolization. Principal limitation: The czar-to-Stalin genealogy is historically-plausible but rests on one case, so it neither establishes that religious-authoritarian conditioning cross-contextually causes secular tyranny nor weighs secular ideology’s independently-originating force. Live burden: Having preserved the narrower claim that credulity enables authoritarian worship, the reply must distinguish inherited religious submission from rival political, institutionally-grounded, and psychologically-grounded explanations of mass obedience. Locked score: 82 rewards the concession, responsiveness, and coherent anti-idolatry inference, while withholding stronger credit because the historically-particular warrant is narrow, the causal generalization evidentially-under-supported, and the rival explanation substantively-unanswered.
